channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Presidente do TSE reúne ministros nesta quinta para tratar de IA e deve discutir ação contra Flávio
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques will meet with ministers this Thursday to discuss the use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns, focusing on the deepfake of Jair Bolsonaro used at the convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro as a presidential candidate. The PT has filed an action requesting judgment on the video, arguing it constitutes illegal early electoral propaganda despite the disclosure that it is a simulation. Flávio Bolsonaro’s defense denies wrongdoing, stating the AI use was transparent and did not amount to an explicit vote solicitation.

item.title: Hugo Motta declara ter R$ 250 mil em dinheiro vivo e apartamento subfaturado em Brasília
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies (Republicanos-PB), declared to electoral justice that he holds R$250,000 in cash outside bank accounts or financial investments, representing 19.8% of his total declared wealth of R$1.26 million. The disclosure has raised concerns about the source of funds and financial transparency, as the amount is kept outside the formal banking system. This is not the first time Motta has faced scrutiny over his asset declarations.

item.title: A repercussão nas redes do primeiro debate entre Tarcísio e Haddad
item.description: The first debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad for the São Paulo gubernatorial race generated over 6 million social media interactions in 24 hours, with 'Haddad' and 'Tarcísio' ranking among the top five trending topics on X. The term 'debate band' reached 12th place on Google Trends, peaking at 7:56 p.m. on Sunday, indicating strong public engagement.

item.title: O debate entre candidatos muda votos?
item.description: A survey of 664 readers found that 36.3% believe candidate debates change votes, 33.3% say they do not, and 30.4% think it only happens in exceptional cases. The content also includes pieces about Flávio’s fear of becoming a target of the right in Lula’s absence from the studio, as well as articles on anti-antifa movements and political satire.

item.title: Temendo “queimar a largada”, Planalto vai manter Berger no cargo
item.description: The Planalto has decided to keep Swedenberger Barbosa (Berger) in office despite speculation about his involvement with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, to avoid premature action before concrete evidence emerges. Investigators are probing whether Berger facilitated the release of Health Ministry funds to the Maranhão government, similar to the case of former chief of staff Marcola, who received R$249,000 from Luchsinger and was removed from Lula's campaign.

item.title: Planalto descarta 'medida de força' dos EUA contra Lula, mas prevê pressão
item.description: The Brazilian federal government ruled out the possibility of the United States applying a 'force measure' against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but acknowledged that diplomatic and political pressures could occur. The concern arose after a U.S. Republican lawmaker shared a montage depicting Lula imprisoned, which was labeled as a symptom of the 'deteriorated political environment' internationally. The Planalto Palace emphasized respect for U.S. sovereignty while rejecting any attempt to intimidate democratically elected leaders.

item.title: Ao evitar debate, Lula tenta transferir alvo para as costas de Flávio
item.description: Lula has not yet rejected Band's invitation to the electoral debate, but in the campaign, no one is advocating for his participation in the first-round debates. The assessment is that by avoiding the debate, he aims to shift the target of criticism onto Flávio Dino, his Justice Minister, as a way to protect his own image and indirectly wear down the opponent.

item.title: Pesquisa: Metade dos eleitores sem religião saturou da polarização política
item.description: BTG/Nexus poll shows half of religiously unaffiliated voters in Brazil are weary of political polarization, while evangelicals report greater tolerance, stating the divide does not affect their candidate choices in the October elections.

item.title: Excesso de cautela no defeso eleitoral provoca ‘apagão’ e especialistas citam riscos à transparência
item.description: The federal government directed the removal of content from ministries and public agencies during the electoral blackout to avoid accusations of using public resources to benefit Lula’s re-election campaign. This guidance led to excessive caution, causing a 'data blackout' where pages and posts were removed indiscriminately, threatening public transparency. Experts warn that while intended to shield the government, the measure undermines access to information and may constitute preventive censorship.

item.title: ​Alvo da PF, Weverton vê candidatura ao Senado em xeque, e Brandão avalia chapa sem contrariar Lula
item.description: Governor Carlos Brandão is evaluating with his inner circle whether to keep Senator Weverton Rocha on the Senate ticket after the lawmaker was targeted in another Federal Police operation linked to the INSS scandal, raising concerns about electoral contamination for his nephew Orleans Brandão’s gubernatorial bid. Despite the investigative fallout, the group hesitates to drop Weverton due to direct pressure from President Lula, who endorsed him and enjoys over 70% support in Maranhão. With the candidate registration deadline this Saturday, there is insufficient time to conduct polls to inform the decision.

item.title: Charge do Aroeira
item.description: The Aroeira cartoon depicts Flávio Bolsonaro worried about becoming a target of the right itself, even without Lula present in the studio. It suggests internal tensions within the Bolsonarist base, with risk of political isolation despite traditional support. The image critiques the fragility of ideological unity within the Brazilian right.

item.title: Governo Lula prepara ato de 200 dias do Pacto contra Feminicídio
item.description: The Lula government is preparing an event to mark the 200-day milestone of the National Pact Against Femicide, highlighting recent advances and coordinated actions across government branches and levels. Scheduled for the first half of September, the ceremony aims to strengthen Lula’s campaign by showcasing gender equality policies and efforts to combat structural machismo. The initiative unfolds amid electoral competition, particularly with FL Bolsonaro (PL), who also seeks to attract female voters.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio busca líderes para avançar entre evangélicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign has launched a targeted effort to improve his standing among evangelical voters, aiming to reduce rejection and increase support in this key demographic. The strategy involves meetings with religious leaders, participation in church-linked WhatsApp groups, communication coaching, and scheduled appearances at religious events, such as a recent service at the Igreja Mundial do Poder de Deus in São Paulo. Although he identifies as evangelical and has undergone multiple baptisms—including one in the Jordan River—the campaign seeks to ensure he is perceived as such by voters, with backing from figures like Deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante and outreach to the evangelical bloc in Congress.

item.title: Após convenções, Renan e JHC seguem com chapas em aberto em Alagoas
item.description: Party conventions in Alagoas failed to finalize majoritarian tickets, leaving JHC (PSDB) and Renan Filho (MDB) with open candidacies. JHC did not formally declare his gubernatorial bid, though the PSDB/Cidadania federation named him as their candidate, delegating the final decision to the Executive Committee by August 15. Renan Filho, despite indicating a running mate at the convention, remains in negotiations, while JHC’s allies have already endorsed Ronaldo Lessa (PDT) for vice.

item.title: Sem Lula no estúdio, Flávio teme virar o alvo da própria direita
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula are adopting the same tactical approach of avoiding first-round debates, fearing they would become isolated targets of attacks from within their own right-wing coalition or from all opponents combined. Flávio insists he will only debate if Lula is present, while Lula considers skipping to avoid being ganged up on. Ricardo Noblat highlights the hypocrisy, noting that Caiado — who calls Flávio a 'coward' — himself avoided nearly all debates in 2022 when leading in polls for re-election in Goiás.

item.title: Ex-prefeito condenado por fraude em BRT foi assessor de deputado do PT
item.description: The former mayor of São José dos Campos, Carlinhos de Almeida (PT), convicted of diverting R$14.5 million in a non-existent BRT project, served as an advisor to state deputy Emídio de Souza (PT) for over seven years, earning between R$8,800 and R$22,800 monthly, totaling over R$1.5 million. Despite his TJSP conviction, he remained in the role for two months after the ruling, claiming he was preparing his defense. Souza is a close ally of Lula and coordinates Fernando Haddad’s campaign for governor of São Paulo.

item.title: Lula recicla promessas de campanha em novo programa de governo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 2026 government program recycles unfulfilled 2022 campaign promises, including the creation of a Ministry of Public Security and regulation of app-based work. The new ministry depends on a stalled Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) in the Senate, while platform labor regulation was postponed after being sent to Congress in March 2024. The document emphasizes coordinating security policies with federal entities and establishing labor rights in the digital economy.

item.title: Flávio reúne candidatos ao Senado em ofensiva por maioria na Casa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro gathers Senate candidates from the PL and allied parties to align messaging and build a Senate majority, aiming to strengthen his presidential campaign and influence congressional and Supreme Court decisions. The meeting in Brasília, expected to draw around 40 candidates, focuses on post-2027 Senate composition and the chamber's role in approving Supreme Court nominees.

item.title: Brasil visto de São Paulo
item.description: The debate between Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and former Minister Fernando Haddad, despite deep ideological differences, was marked by both candidates’ presence and the absence of personal attacks. Although Tarcísio leads in polls and Haddad harbors strong aversion to Bolsonarism, the two treated each other as legitimate adversaries in a decisive national contest, offering voters a civilized exchange free from fear of violence or chaos. The article highlights that dialogue between opponents is a relief for Brazilian democracy.

item.title: Sem Kassab, MDB e grupo ligado a Nunes tocam campanha de Tarcísio
item.description: The re-election campaign of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) in São Paulo is being coordinated by MDB figures linked to Mayor Ricardo Nunes, such as Vitor Arruda and Diogo Soares, following the distancing from Gilberto Kassab (PSD). Roberto Carneiro, state president of the Republicans, leads the political coordination. Although the PSD remains officially in the coalition, it has lost influence due to disagreements over the vice-presidential pick and Kassab’s focus on Ronaldo Caiado’s presidential campaign.

item.title: A mudança de tom de Alcolumbre sobre a indicação de Lula ao STF
item.description: Allies of Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) say the Senate president has shifted his tone regarding the potential Lula nominee to the STF, showing greater openness to dialogue. The subscriber-only article suggests a change in posture that could influence the selection process for the new justice.

item.title: A resistência na PF à nota de superintendentes em defesa de Andrei Rodrigues
item.description: Despite a note of support signed by 27 Federal Police superintendents for director-general Andrei Rodrigues, there was internal resistance to the statement, which emerged amid tensions with STF Minister André Mendonça over investigations into billion-dollar fraud schemes in INSS and Banco Master, both highly relevant to the 2026 elections.

item.title: Esquerda, centro ou direita? Teste ideológico do GLOBO indica a sua posição política
item.description: GLOBO launched an ideological test based on the Nolan Chart, adapted to the Brazilian context with consultation from Professor Emerson Cervi of UFPR. The quiz evaluates positions on economic, social, and cultural issues through questions on topics like gun ownership, abortion, privatization, and university quotas, classifying users as left, center-left, center, center-right, or right. Launched two months before the 2026 elections, it aims to measure ideological consistency among citizens.

item.title: Liberação de empréstimos federais turbina embate entre Tarcísio e Haddad em São Paulo
item.description: The debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad on Band was marked by mutual accusations over alleged federal blockades on loan disbursements for São Paulo, with the Republican governor criticizing delays and the former finance minister defending Lula’s management. The initially state-level dispute gained national traction after being taken up by Flávio Bolsonaro, linking it to the 2026 presidential race. Though not fully detailed in the accessible excerpt, the issue reflects fiscal and political tensions between São Paulo’s and the federal governments.

item.title: Ministros do TSE indicam possível multa por vídeo de Bolsonaro com IA e devem calibrar decisão para servir de precedente
item.description: TSE ministers indicate that the AI-generated video of Bolsonaro declaring support for Flávio Bolsonaro should result in a fine for violating electoral propaganda rules, not harsher sanctions like registration cancellation. The decision aims to set a clear precedent for AI use in campaigns, distinguishing minor violations from abuse of power or recidivism to prevent an overload on electoral justice.

item.title: Lula de chapéu: aliados temem questionamentos após campanha registrar foto do presidente com o adereço para a urna
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election campaign submitted a ballot photo showing him wearing a Panama hat, raising concerns among allies about potential legal challenges at the TSE. Lula has worn the hat since April, following skin cancer treatment, as a medical recommendation to avoid sun exposure. Although unusual, the campaign cites precedents, such as the 2022 case of Douglas Belchior, where the TSE allowed a cap because it did not hinder voter recognition.

item.title: Flávio deixa registro de candidatura para reta final do prazo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) chose to file his presidential candidacy on Thursday (8/13), just two days before the final registration deadline (8/15), despite holding his party convention earlier. His team stated they are still finalizing details such as documentation and ballot box photos. As of Monday (8/10), five candidates had already registered, including Lula, who filed on Friday (8/7).

item.title: Polarização cansa mais eleitores com ensino superior, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: Political polarization is causing fatigue or discomfort among Brazilian voters with higher education, according to a BTG/Nexus poll. The data shows that 52% of those with college education report feeling tired or uneasy about the political divide affecting presidential elections. The analysis indicates this weariness is more pronounced among more educated segments of the electorate.

item.title: "Brasileiros não confiam nas urnas eletrônicas", diz CEO do Instituto IDEIA
item.description: Cila Schulman, CEO of the IDEIA Institute, states that a significant portion of the Brazilian population distrusts the integrity of electronic voting machines, despite the absence of evidence of fraud. She notes that this skepticism is particularly prevalent among voters of Flávio Bolsonaro and cites OEA data indicating that nationwide electoral fraud would be statistically extremely difficult, requiring the manipulation of 5,000 voting machines with 100% of votes for a single candidate to shift the outcome by just 1%.

item.title: Justiça do Rio determina que Garotinho cumpra sentença e informa suspensão de direitos políticos a tribunais eleitorais
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's judiciary ordered former governor Anthony Garotinho to serve a sentence for administrative misconduct linked to the 'Saúde em Movimento' program (2005-2006), following the exhaustion of appeals at the STF. The ruling mandates notification of his eight-year political rights suspension to the TSE and TRE-RJ, while clarifying that only electoral courts can determine eligibility. Garotinho's defense contests the decision, asserting he remains in full exercise of his political rights until his candidacy is formally judged.

item.title: Não pode haver retrocesso na reforma tributária
item.description: The article criticizes the campaign promises of Flávio Bolsonaro and Ronaldo Caiado to revise the 2023 tax reform, calling them irresponsible. The reform unified consumption taxes after decades of debate and included a ten-year transition period for adaptation. Electoral pressures from dissatisfied groups threaten to roll back progress aimed at ending Brazil’s tax complexity and attracting investment.

item.title: Em corrida ao Planalto, Lula eleva o tom contra emendas do Congresso e Flávio intensifica críticas ao STF
item.description: Lula intensified criticism of parliamentary amendments, calling them a distortion of the federal budget and proposing reforms to reduce their impact on public management. Flávio Bolsonaro, meanwhile, increased his attacks on the STF, calling Alexandre de Moraes' decision to deny him a visit to former President Jair Bolsonaro on Father's Day 'inhumane'. Both pre-candidates are targeting democratic institutions as campaign focal points, escalating tensions between the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches.

item.title: Quaest: 20% dos eleitores afirmam que decidem voto para presidente na última semana
item.description: A Quaest poll shows that 20% of voters decide their presidential vote in the final week, including 10% on election day. For senatorial votes, this rises to 32%, with 14% deciding on the day of voting. Presidential voting is the most anticipated, with 58% deciding months in advance, while independent voters show greater indecision, with only 41% deciding early.

item.title: Banco Central detalha hoje corte da Selic para 14% em ata do Copom
item.description: The Central Bank released the Copom minutes confirming the Selic rate cut to 14%, the lowest since early 2025, following four consecutive reductions in the easing cycle that began in March. The statement emphasized caution amid global volatility, including Middle East conflict, Brazilian elections, and climate risks, reiterating that future decisions will depend on incoming data without signaling plans for upcoming meetings. Analysts await the minutes to calibrate expectations for the September 16 meeting, with markets split between another 0.25-point cut to 13.75% or holding at 14%.

item.title: André do Prado registra candidatura ao Senado por SP e declara patrimônio 81% maior que em 2022
item.description: State deputy André do Prado (PL), president of the São Paulo Legislative Assembly, had his Senate candidacy registered by the TSE on April 7. He declared assets worth R$ 692,6 thousand, 81% higher than in 2022, according to his electoral financial disclosure.

item.title: Citada por Haddad para criticar Smart Sampa, pensão alimentícia é bandeira de Lula
item.description: Fernando Haddad mentioned child support payments during the TV Band debate to downplay the importance of the Smart Sampa program, emphasizing that the issue is a priority of the Lula government and part of the president’s electoral platform. Child support is framed as a social protection and family justice banner, aligned with the PT’s 2026 proposals.

item.title: A maior preocupação de Lula e Flávio no primeiro ato de campanha
item.description: The size of the crowd at the first campaign events of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro has become a strategic concern, as aerial images of the gatherings may be interpreted as signs of electoral strength or weakness. Lula aims to gather 25,000 people in São Bernardo do Campo to avoid giving opponents ammunition to portray weakness, while Flávio faces the challenge of Copacabana’s vast expanse, which can make even a large crowd appear sparse in aerial footage, risking a perception of low turnout.

item.title: Celina oferece Brasília para sediar final da Copa do Brasil 2026
item.description: The Governor of the Federal District, Celina Leão (PP), sent a letter to the CBF requesting that the 2026 Copa do Brasil final be held at the Estádio Nacional Mané Garrincha in Brasília, citing the stadium’s modern infrastructure, logistical capacity, hotel network, and central location as key advantages. She also reiterated the GDF’s interest in maintaining Brasília as a permanent host venue for future editions due to its proven experience in large-scale events and national significance.

item.title: Temas nacionais vão monopolizar debates regionais
item.description: The 2026 gubernatorial debates in São Paulo were dominated by nationalized themes, with Fernando Haddad (PT) and Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) aligning their campaigns with Lula and Bolsonaro, respectively. Haddad, trailing in polls, seeks to nationalize the race to leverage Lula’s support, while Bolsonaro views Tarcísio as a key ally to strengthen his influence in São Paulo. Nationalizing the debate benefits both candidates—but for opposite reasons: Haddad needs it to survive; Tarcísio uses it to advance his national project under the bolsonarist banner.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos ao governo de SP nas eleições de 2026?
item.description: The 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial race will feature six candidates officially defined in party conventions held between July and August. The list includes Carlos Machado (PCB), Fernando Haddad (PT), Izadora Dias (PCO), Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), Vera Lúcia (PSTU) and Vivian Mendes (UP), with the first round scheduled for October 4 and a potential runoff on October 25. Proposals range from re-nationalization of public services and strengthening education and health to continuity of current administration policies.

item.title: Três diagnósticos sobre a disputa Lula x Flávio após pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula at 40% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 35% in the first round, and 47% to 44% in the second round, indicating a technical tie. Flávio Bolsonaro is seen as competitive and resilient despite challenges such as limited political support and controversies. Other candidates remain stagnant below 5%, while Lula appears to have reached an electoral ceiling around 47%.

item.title: Rogério Marinho critica atuação do STF e diz que Corte precisa voltar a ser constitucional
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) criticized the Supreme Federal Court's actions, stating it has acted like a 'police station' instead of fulfilling its constitutional role. He urged the STF to return to being a constitutional court and for each branch to respect its duties, particularly criticizing meetings between STF ministers and President Lula as inappropriate and normalized. Marinho also discussed impeachment of ministers, saying it should only apply in cases of proven responsibility crimes, noting he has signed such requests before but they did not advance in Congress.

item.title: Juiz determina que Garotinho cumpra sentença que suspende direitos políticos
item.description: Judge Ricardo Cyfer ordered the enforcement of a sentence suspending former Rio de Janeiro governor Anthony Garotinho's political rights for 8 years, after the STF denied his appeal. The ruling requires the Electoral Justice to assess his ineligibility, stemming from an administrative improbity conviction involving R$ 234.4 million in damages and a civil fine.

item.title: Em novo ataque, Milei compartilha postagem em que aliado de Trump chama Lula de 'porco'
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei shared a post by a U.S. Republican congressman who called Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a 'pig', escalating diplomatic tensions between the two nations. Milei had previously labeled Lula a 'thief', 'corrupt', and 'convict', defending his remarks as justified criticism of corruption and socialism, and praised Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign as a bulwark against the influence of the São Paulo Forum. The Brazilian government has not issued a direct response, but bilateral relations remain highly strained.

item.title: Lindbergh é acusado de forjar acusação de estupro contra Alfredo Gaspar; deputado petista nega
item.description: Deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) accused Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) of fabricating a rape allegation against him, based on testimony from a merchant who claimed payments were made to sustain the false claim. Lindbergh denies the allegations and filed a lawsuit at the STF to suspend the Federal Legislative Police investigation, while the PF received a request to open an inquiry into Gaspar for rape of a vulnerable person, pending further information from the PGR.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pressiona deputada Ana Campagnolo e condiciona uso de imagem a apoio a Carlos em SC
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro pressured state deputy Ana Campagnolo to record a video supporting his brother Carlos Bolsonaro’s Senate campaign in Santa Catarina, conditioning the use of his and Jair Bolsonaro’s images on her compliance. Campagnolo stated the video was filmed in May without prior agreement and affirmed her alignment with the PL’s stance in SC, offering to support the party’s majority ticket. Carlos Bolsonaro’s candidacy had already caused discomfort within the PL in SC due to his long tenure in Rio de Janeiro and the broader bolsonarist strategy to leverage SC’s strong Bolsonaro base from 2022.

item.title: As cidades que pesam muito na decisão eleitoral em São Paulo, segundo cientista político
item.description: Political scientist Fábio Vasconcellos identified 18 swing cities in São Paulo that alternated support between left and right from 2002 to 2022, concentrating over 90% of the state's electorate. The analysis shows nearly 75% of municipalities vote more often for right-wing candidates, while the PT has stronger presence in smaller towns. The metropolitan region, including São Paulo, Guarulhos, São Bernardo do Campo, and Osasco, holds the greatest weight among these swing municipalities, with 13% shifting between 2018 and 2022, significantly contributing to Lula's 2022 victory.

item.title: “Flávio Bolsonaro e Zema estão no nosso palanque”, diz Van Hattem
item.description: Marcel van Hattem, Novo party candidate for Senate in Rio Grande do Sul, said he maintains independence from presidential candidates and denied being subordinate to national slates. He stated that, nationally, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Romeu Zema (Novo) will be together against the PT on a common slate, although his party remains autonomous.

item.title: Ex-deputado desiste de ser vice do candidato de Flávio Bolsonaro em Minas
item.description: Former federal deputy Charlles Evangelista (PL) withdrew as the vice-gubernatorial candidate on Flávio Roscoe’s (PL) ticket in Minas Gerais, which is backed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, announcing his decision via Instagram. He chose to pursue his own campaign for a federal congressional seat, stating he wants to continue a political project aligned with his core issues. Evangelista also expressed support for the candidacy of Sheila Aparecida Oliveira (Delegada Sheila) for state deputy.

item.title: O que Milei pode ensinar a Lula sobre economia, afinal
item.description: The article examines what Brazil can learn from Argentina's fiscal adjustment under Javier Milei, noting that despite a severe 27% cut in public spending, Argentina avoided economic collapse and achieved 4.4% GDP growth in 2024. Economist Fabio Giambiagi argues that Brazil requires a much milder adjustment, advocating for capping public spending growth at 4-5% annually instead of current Lula 3 levels, while warning about democratic limits to austerity measures.
